skill.name: file-organizer
skill.description: Organizes folders by analyzing files, finding duplicates, proposing safer structures, and applying approved cleanup steps.
skill.summary: Guides safe folder cleanup, duplicate review, and file organization plans.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: All 56 static alerts were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline path examples, or plain text organization guidance. The skill includes user-approved filesystem inspection and organization workflows, but I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration, unauthorized network access, or automatic destructive behavior.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use broad placeholders for target directories.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to choose a narrow directory, preview actions, and confirm every move or deletion.

remediation.issue: Duplicate cleanup can cause data loss if users act too quickly.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend archiving duplicate candidates before deletion and keeping a move log for rollback.

content.value_statement: Messy folders and duplicate files make work harder and waste storage. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through safe analysis, planning, and approved file organization.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a target directory and summarizes file types, sizes, dates, and structure.
Suggests folder structures by file type, purpose, date, or project status.
Finds exact duplicates, same-name files, and similar-sized files for review.
Drafts a step-by-step move, rename, archive, or cleanup plan before changes.
Provides maintenance tips and naming conventions for organized folders.
limitations: Requires user approval before destructive actions; it should not delete files automatically.
Shell examples may need adjustment for Windows, macOS, or Linux command differences.
Cannot know personal context for ambiguous files without user decisions.
May need broad filesystem access to analyze large folders, which can expose sensitive file names.

use_cases.title: Clean a Downloads Folder
use_cases.description: Sort mixed downloads into useful folders, identify old installers, and flag files that need decisions.

use_cases.title: Audit Shared Project Files
use_cases.description: Review project folders, separate active and archived work, and suggest consistent naming rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare Archives for Backup
use_cases.description: Group old files by date or purpose before backup, migration, or storage cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Organize One Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for a single messy folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize my Downloads folder conservatively. First summarize what is there, then propose folders, and ask before moving or deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicate Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate files in my Documents folder. Show each duplicate group with sizes and dates, recommend which copy to keep, and wait for my decision.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Project Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a project workspace with active and archived work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Projects folder and propose a clearer structure for active work, archived projects, templates, and learning files. Do not change files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup across multiple folders with constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged cleanup plan for Downloads, Desktop, and Documents. Exclude sensitive folders, keep a rollback log, archive before deletion, and ask for approval at each stage.

output_examples.input: My Downloads folder has hundreds of mixed files. Help me clean it up.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the folder, groups files by purpose, proposes folders such as Work, Personal, Installers, Archive, and To Review, then asks before moving anything.

output_examples.input: Find duplicates in Documents and tell me what to keep.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists duplicate sets with file names, sizes, dates, and recommended keepers. It asks for confirmation before removing or archiving copies.

output_examples.input: Review my project directories and suggest improvements.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies active, archived, template, and learning projects, then proposes a cleaner structure with a staged migration plan.

best_practices: Start with one target folder and request a dry-run plan before changes.
Mark sensitive, active, or shared folders as off limits before analysis.
Archive uncertain files before deletion and keep a log of moved files.
anti_patterns: Running broad cleanup across the whole home directory without scope limits.
Deleting duplicate files before confirming which copy is authoritative.
Applying one naming rule to mixed personal, work, and project files.

faq.question: Does this skill delete files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to ask for confirmation before deletion and to prefer archiving when uncertain.

faq.question: Can it organize photos?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose year and month folders using file dates or available photo metadata.

faq.question: Can it find duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare hashes, file names, sizes, and dates, then present duplicate groups for review.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared work folders?
faq.answer: Use a narrow scope and confirm with the team before moving shared files or changing naming rules.

faq.question: Does it work on every operating system?
faq.answer: The workflow is portable, but some shell commands may need platform-specific changes.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Choose a target folder, list any off-limits files, and decide how conservative the cleanup should be.
